source.title: Spend Less, Fit Better: Budget-Efficient Scaling Law Fitting via Active Experiment Selection
source.authors: Si-Jie Li; Shan-Da Li; Hao-Wei Lin; Wei-Wei Sun; A. Talwalkar; Yi-Ming Yang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates how accurately fitted scaling laws extrapolate to held-out, high-cost target regions using different selections of training experiments. This bears on extrapolation, but it does not reproduce the original studies’ scaling-law measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates target-region R² for fitted laws across benchmark tasks and budget levels. Its task-level values aggregate over multiple scaling-law instances. It does not report direct measurements of loss versus parameter count, tokens, or compute, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.test_reason: This is mainly a method paper: budget-aware selection of runs for fitting scaling laws. Its SL2-versus-baseline numbers measure how well the selection method works, not whether scaling laws extrapolate. Two of its reference results do bear on V2: All Data (the law fitted on the whole small-run pool, scored on the held-out high-cost target region) and the cheap-half fits. Per-law All Data R² across law families (Table 6) also bears on V7. The data are reanalysed from SLDBench and the source papers, so this is a different method aimed at the same question (T2).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SL2 generally outperforms random, heuristic and design-based baselines and often approaches full-data performance at about 10% of the budget. They also say that fitting all pilot runs can be suboptimal for predicting much larger configurations, and that SL2 may fail under severe misspecification such as unseen phase transitions.
record.recipe_differences: Budget-aware sequential selection of experiments and target-region R² evaluation across existing scaling-law benchmark instances; not a replication of the original scaling-law experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Extrapolation performance varies by benchmark task and budget. Experiment-selection strategy affects results; cost-penalty exponent and warm-start size are also varied in robustness analyses.

fits_no_version.finding: Which runs are selected for fitting strongly changes the accuracy of target-region extrapolation at a fixed budget. SL2 and V-opt beat Random and Cheapest, and fitting all data can be worse than a selected subset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling-law extrapolation accuracy depends on how the pilot runs are chosen, not only on how many there are or what they cost.

record.problems: Benchmark results aggregate over heterogeneous scaling-law instances, and task-level performance varies substantially. The paper itself warns that severe model misspecification, especially unobserved abrupt phase transitions, can undermine extrapolation. The reported target-region R² results do not directly establish extrapolation across orders of magnitude.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 also reports results for Random, Cheapest, Cost Rand, D-opt, V-opt, and All Data, plus 10% (or task-specific 50%) budget results. These were not extracted to keep the record focused on the main SL2 small-budget outcomes; the paper's aggregate comparison and conclusion are noted above.

untested.parts: The text does not state how many orders of magnitude separate the target region from the pilot runs. Several law families include hyperparameters or other variables rather than parameters, tokens or compute alone.
Fitted exponents and compute-optimal splits are not reported. Dependence is shown only through target-region R² across law families and run selections.

missing.what: All Data target-region R² per task: lr&bsz 0.04, domain 0.81, vocab 0.93, parallel 0.99, moe 0.81, data con 0.79, sparsity 0.37, farseer 0.91.
Cheap-half vs expensive-half fits, target-region R². Cheap half: lr&bsz -0.89, vocab 0.84, parallel 1.00, moe 0.42, data con 0.54, sparsity -0.67, farseer 0.51.
Per-law All Data test R² showing a wide spread across law families within each task.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the study's own-method rows to V2. These show selection-method performance, not whether laws extrapolate, so they are relinked to none. The evidence relevant to V2 and V7 is in the All Data reference results, the cheap/expensive-half diagnostic and Table 6; verdicts rest on these text results. The domain task (mixture proportions, unit cost) is not scaling and is excluded. The data are reanalysed from SLDBench and the source papers, not new training runs.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out loss as a power law in parameters, tokens, or compute.

Tests target-region extrapolation from budgeted subsets of experiments, but does not establish that the target runs are orders of magnitude larger or report a direct small-run-versus-large-run loss comparison.
Does not determine loss-minimising parameter and token allocations as a function of compute.
Does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Does not test the same power-law form across modalities or other training regimes.

It varies experiment-selection strategy and examines fit/extrapolation performance, but does not report changes in fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits, nor test whether curves bend away from a single power law.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: parallel, vocab, farseer, moe and data con laws fitted on the full small-run pool
source_check.reason: Table 3 reports All Data target-region R² means of 0.99, 0.93, 0.91, 0.81 and 0.79, respectively. This supports prediction in these benchmark settings at the task-average level.

relationships.condition: sparsity laws; and fits using only the cheap half of the pool (moe, farseer, data con)
relationships.reason: Text-based: sparsity All Data R² is 0.37. Cheap-half fits fall to 0.42, 0.51 and 0.54 on moe, farseer and data con (Table 4).
relationships.display_finding: Sparsity-law R² was 0.37 using all data; fitting only the cheaper half yielded R² of 0.42 for mixture-of-experts, 0.51 for Farseer, and 0.54 for data-constrained experiments.

source_check.condition: sparsity laws; and fits using only the cheap half of the pool (moe, farseer, data con)
source_check.reason: Table 3 gives sparsity All Data R² 0.37. Table 4 gives cheap-half R² 0.42 for moe, 0.51 for farseer and 0.54 for data con, showing incomplete extrapolation under these conditions.

relationships.reason: Text-based: lr&bsz All Data R² is 0.04, and cheap-half R² is -0.89 (lr&bsz) and -0.67 (sparsity). Small runs fail to predict the target region.
relationships.display_finding: Step Law R² was 0.04 using all data, while fitting only the cheaper half yielded R² of -0.89 for learning-rate/batch-size experiments and -0.67 for sparsity.

relation.reason: Tables 3–4 directly evaluate whether fitted laws predict loss in the extrapolation region.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates held-out, high-cost-region loss predictions using different experiment-selection and fitting procedures. Its full-pool and half-pool reference fits provide extrapolation evidence beyond its method comparisons.

source_check.notes: Tables 3–4 report task aggregates over heterogeneous law families; Table 3 R² is clipped to [−1, 1]. The V2 evidence concerns high-cost extrapolation, but the cited tables do not establish an orders-of-magnitude scale separation or isolate classical power laws.
